tasks.title: Isolate Existing Gatsby Project
tasks.description: Move Gatsby-specific files and directories (configs, src, static, content, package.json) into a 'gatsby/' subdirectory to prepare for Next.js installation at the root.
tasks.details:
1. Create a 'gatsby/' directory.
2. Move gatsby-*.js config files into 'gatsby/'.
3. Move 'src/', 'static/', 'content/' directories into 'gatsby/'.
4. Move 'package.json' and 'package-lock.json' to 'gatsby/' (e.g., as package.json.old).
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that all essential Gatsby project files are inside the 'gatsby/' directory and the root directory is clean for Next.js installation.

tasks.title: Initialize Next.js Project with Tailwind CSS
tasks.description: Set up a new Next.js project with Tailwind CSS and configure essential development tools.
tasks.details:
1. Run `npx create-next-app@latest . --ts --eslint --tailwind --src-dir --app --use-npm --no-customize-alias` in the project root.
2. Verify the basic project structure is created.
3. Confirm Tailwind CSS is configured correctly.
4. Ensure ESLint and TypeScript setups are functional.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `npm run dev` and ensure the default Next.js page loads without errors. Check for the presence of `tailwind.config.js`, `tsconfig.json`, and `.eslintrc.json`.

tasks.title: Configure Core Layout and Styling
tasks.description: Set up the main application layout, global styles, and integrate Tailwind CSS.
tasks.details:
1. Create a root layout component in `src/app/layout.tsx`.
2. Import global CSS (including Tailwind directives) in the root layout.
3. Define basic page structure (header, main content area, footer) within the layout.
4. Apply initial Tailwind classes for typography, background, etc. Set up Google Fonts 'PT Serif' and 'Fira Code' using `next/font`.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify the basic layout structure appears on the home page. Check that Tailwind utility classes are being applied correctly. Verify fonts load.

tasks.title: Implement Markdown Content Processing
tasks.description: Set up utilities to read and parse Markdown blog posts from the `gatsby/content/blog` directory.
tasks.details:
1. Install necessary libraries: `gray-matter`, `remark`, `remark-html`.
2. Create utility functions in `src/lib/posts.ts` (or similar) to:
   - Read files from `gatsby/content/blog`.
   - Parse frontmatter using `gray-matter`.
   - Convert Markdown content to HTML using `remark`.
   - Generate slugs from filenames (e.g., removing date prefixes).
tasks.testStrategy: Write unit tests for the utility functions. Test reading a sample Markdown file and verify correct parsing of frontmatter and HTML content generation.

tasks.title: Create Blog Index Page
tasks.description: Build the main page (`/`) to list all blog posts.
tasks.details:
1. Create the main page component at `src/app/page.tsx`.
2. Use the content processing utilities (Task 4) to fetch sorted post data (slug, title, date, excerpt).
3. Render a list of post previews, each linking to the post's future dynamic route.
4. Apply Tailwind CSS for styling the list and previews.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify the home page loads and displays a list of posts fetched from the Markdown files. Check that links point to the correct slug paths (e.g., `/blog/[slug]`).

tasks.title: Create Dynamic Blog Post Pages
tasks.description: Build the template to display individual blog posts at `/blog/[slug]`.
tasks.details:
1. Create the dynamic route page component at `src/app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx`.
2. Implement `generateStaticParams` to define all possible blog post slugs.
3. Implement the page component to fetch full post data (including HTML content) for a given slug using Task 4 utilities.
4. Render the post title, metadata, and HTML content using `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Handle image path resolution/optimization (`next/image`). Handle code blocks.
5. \nApply Tailwind CSS for post styling.
tasks.testStrategy: Navigate to individual blog post URLs. Verify title, metadata, and content render correctly. Ensure basic Markdown formatting (headings, lists, code blocks, images) is preserved.

tasks.title: Implement RSS Feed Generation
tasks.description: Create an RSS feed at `/rss.xml` containing all blog posts.
tasks.details:
1. Create an API route handler (e.g., `src/app/rss.xml/route.ts`).
2. Use the content processing utilities (Task 4) to fetch all post data.
3. Install and use a library like `feed`.
4. Generate the RSS feed XML with appropriate channel info and post items.
5. Return the XML with the correct content type header.
tasks.testStrategy: Access `/rss.xml` in the browser or via curl. Validate the feed using an online validator. Ensure all posts are included with correct links and metadata.

tasks.title: Implement Sitemap and Robots.txt Generation
tasks.details:
1. **Sitemap:** Create an API route handler (e.g., `src/app/sitemap.xml/route.ts`) that generates an XML sitemap including the home page and all blog post pages with last modification dates.
2. **Robots.txt:** Create a static file `public/robots.txt` with appropriate rules, potentially referencing the sitemap.
tasks.testStrategy: Access `/sitemap.xml` and `/robots.txt` directly. Verify correct formatting and inclusion of all relevant URLs. Validate the sitemap using an online validator.

tasks.title: Migrate Static Pages and Assets
tasks.description: Migrate any non-blog static pages (e.g., About) and handle static assets.
tasks.details:
1. Identify static pages in the original `gatsby/src/pages`.
2. Create corresponding page components in `src/app/` (e.g., `src/app/about/page.tsx`).
3. Move required static assets (images, fonts) from `gatsby/static` to the Next.js `public/` directory.
4. Update asset references in components and styles.
5. Apply Tailwind CSS for styling.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify static pages render correctly with proper styling and assets.

tasks.title: Implement SEO Components and Metadata
tasks.description: Create SEO components to handle page titles, meta descriptions, and Open Graph tags.
tasks.details:
1. Create an SEO component or utilize Next.js Metadata API in layouts/pages.
2. Implement dynamic metadata for blog posts based on frontmatter.
3. Add Open Graph tags for social sharing.
tasks.testStrategy: Use browser dev tools to inspect head elements. Test with social media preview tools.

tasks.title: Configure Deployment and Analytics
tasks.description: Configure Netlify deployment settings and potentially set up analytics.
tasks.details:
1. Update `netlify.toml` with Next.js build command (`npm run build`) and publish directory (`.next`).
2. Configure environment variables in Netlify if needed.
3. Add any necessary redirects or headers in `netlify.toml` or `next.config.js`.
4. Optionally, integrate an analytics solution.
tasks.testStrategy: Trigger a deploy preview build on Netlify. Verify successful build and deployment. Test the deployed preview site thoroughly.

tasks.title: Refine Styling and Visual Parity
tasks.description: Review and refine Tailwind CSS styling across the site to ensure visual parity with the original Gatsby site.
tasks.details:
1. Compare each page and component with the original site screenshots or live version.
2. Adjust Tailwind classes to fix discrepancies in layout, spacing, typography, and colors.
3. Ensure responsiveness across different screen sizes.
4. Pay attention to details like link states (hover, active), image presentation, and code block styling.
tasks.testStrategy: Perform thorough visual regression testing (manual comparison or using automated tools). Test on multiple browsers and devices.

tasks.title: Migrate Global CSS to Tailwind Utility Classes
tasks.description: Extract and migrate styles from globals.css to inline Tailwind CSS classes across all components, following Tailwind v4 best practices.
tasks.details:
This task involves a systematic migration from global CSS to Tailwind utility classes:

1. **Audit Phase**:
   - Create an inventory of all styles in src/app/globals.css
   - Categorize styles into: layout, typography, colors, animations, responsive styles, etc.
   - Identify which styles have direct Tailwind equivalents and which might need theme extensions
   - Audit which components and pages use each global class (e.g., .wrap, .page-content, .post, .post-header, .meta, .post-content, .site-header, .site-footer, .social-icons, etc.)

2. **Migration Planning**:
   - Create a mapping document that shows each global CSS rule and its Tailwind equivalent
   - Reference the mapping document in docs/globals-css-to-tailwind-mapping.md
   - For each component/page, create a migration checklist mapping each global class to its Tailwind v4 utility equivalent
   - Determine if any styles need to be maintained as CSS variables in the Tailwind config

3. **Implementation**:
   - Update the Tailwind config to include any necessary theme extensions
   - Begin migration with the blog post page ([slug]/page.tsx), demonstrating how to replace each global class with the mapped Tailwind v4 utilities inline
   - Systematically update each component to use Tailwind classes instead of relying on globals.css
   - Repeat for other key components (header, footer, etc.), removing global CSS as each is migrated
   - For complex styles without direct Tailwind equivalents, use the @apply directive in component-specific CSS modules
   - For repeated patterns, consider creating Tailwind component classes in the config

4. **Cleanup**:
   - Remove migrated styles from globals.css
   - Verify no component styling breaks after removal
   - Ensure that any remaining global styles are only those that cannot be represented with Tailwind v4 utilities

Ensure backward compatibility throughout the migration process by implementing and testing changes incrementally.
tasks.testStrategy:
To verify successful migration:

1. **Visual Regression Testing**:
   - Take screenshots of key UI components before migration
   - Compare with post-migration screenshots to ensure visual consistency
   - Test across multiple viewport sizes to verify responsive behavior
   - Test visual parity and responsive behavior after each migration step

2. **Component Testing**:
   - Create a checklist of components affected by globals.css
   - Verify each component renders correctly with Tailwind classes
   - Test component states (hover, focus, active, disabled) to ensure all styles are properly migrated

3. **Browser Compatibility**:
   - Test in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge to ensure cross-browser compatibility
   - Verify mobile rendering on iOS and Android devices

4. **Performance Checks**:
   - Compare bundle sizes before and after migration
   - Measure CSS specificity improvements
   - Verify reduced CSS file size after removing globals.css

5. **Validation Steps**:
   - Run the application with globals.css completely removed to verify no styling dependencies remain
   - Use browser dev tools to confirm styles are applied via Tailwind classes
   - Verify no unexpected CSS cascading issues occur
   - Check for any console errors related to missing styles

subtasks.title: Audit and Inventory Global CSS Styles
subtasks.description: Create a comprehensive inventory of all styles in src/app/globals.css, categorizing them by type and identifying Tailwind v4 equivalents.
subtasks.details:
1. Create a spreadsheet or document with columns for: CSS selector, CSS properties, category (layout, typography, colors, etc.), Tailwind v4 equivalent, and affected components.
2. Analyze globals.css line by line, documenting each style rule.
3. Categorize styles into: layout, typography, colors, spacing, animations, responsive styles, and custom utilities.
4. For each style, identify the direct Tailwind v4 equivalent using the official documentation.
5. Mark styles that don't have direct equivalents for potential theme extension.
6. Use browser developer tools to identify which components are affected by each global style.
7. Document any CSS variables that might need to be preserved in the Tailwind config.
8. Testing approach: Create a visual inventory of key UI elements before migration to use as reference during verification.

subtasks.title: Audit Component and Page Usage of Global Classes
subtasks.description: Identify which components and pages use each global class defined in globals.css to create a comprehensive usage map.
subtasks.details:
1. Create a spreadsheet that maps each global class (e.g., .wrap, .page-content, .post, .post-header, .meta, .post-content, .site-header, .site-footer, .social-icons, etc.) to the components and pages that use it.
2. Use a combination of code search, browser developer tools, and manual inspection to identify all usages.
3. For each global class, document:
   a. The components/pages that use it
   b. How the class is applied (directly, conditionally, dynamically)
   c. Any variations or modifications to the base style
4. Identify patterns of reuse across components to help prioritize migration efforts.
5. Document any dependencies between global classes (e.g., nested selectors or combined selectors).
6. Create a visual reference of how each global class appears in the UI to aid in verification later.
7. Testing approach: Create a test plan that covers all identified components using global classes.

subtasks.title: Configure Tailwind v4 with Theme Extensions
subtasks.description: Set up Tailwind v4 configuration with necessary theme extensions and CSS variables to support the migration from global styles.

subtasks.title: Create Component-Specific Migration Checklists
subtasks.description: For each component and page, create a detailed migration checklist mapping global classes to Tailwind v4 utility equivalents.
subtasks.details:
1. Create a migration checklist template with columns for: global class, affected elements, Tailwind v4 equivalent utilities, migration status, and verification notes.
2. Reference the mapping document in docs/globals-css-to-tailwind-mapping.md for consistent Tailwind equivalents.
3. For each component/page identified in the audit:
   a. List all global classes used by the component
   b. Map each class to its specific Tailwind v4 utility equivalent
   c. Note any component-specific considerations or edge cases
   d. Include before/after code snippets as examples
4. Prioritize components based on complexity and dependencies.
5. Include responsive considerations for each global class (how it behaves at different breakpoints).
6. Document any interactive states (hover, focus, etc.) that need special attention.
7. Testing approach: For each component, define specific visual checks to verify successful migration.

subtasks.title: Migrate Blog Post Page ([slug]/page.tsx)
subtasks.description: Begin the migration process with the blog post page, replacing global classes with mapped Tailwind v4 utilities.
subtasks.details:
1. Use the component-specific migration checklist for the blog post page ([slug]/page.tsx).
2. Take screenshots of the page at various viewport sizes before migration for comparison.
3. Systematically replace each global class with its Tailwind v4 utility equivalent:
   a. .post → [Tailwind equivalent from mapping doc]
   b. .post-header → [Tailwind equivalent from mapping doc]
   c. .meta → [Tailwind equivalent from mapping doc]
   d. .post-content → [Tailwind equivalent from mapping doc]
   e. Any other global classes used by this page
4. Ensure all responsive behaviors are maintained using Tailwind's responsive prefixes.
5. Test the page at various viewport sizes to verify visual parity with the original.
6. Document any challenges or patterns discovered during this migration to inform subsequent component migrations.
7. Testing approach: Compare before/after screenshots and verify all interactive elements and responsive behaviors work as expected.

subtasks.title: Migrate Component Styling to Tailwind Classes
subtasks.description: Systematically update each component to use Tailwind utility classes instead of relying on global CSS styles.
subtasks.details:
1. Following the successful migration of the blog post page, continue with other key components in this order:
   a. Header component (site-header)
   b. Footer component (site-footer)
   c. Social icons component (social-icons)
   d. Other components based on the prioritized list
2. For each component:
   a. Reference its specific migration checklist created in subtask 7
   b. Replace class references with equivalent Tailwind utility classes
   c. Test the component in isolation and in context to ensure visual consistency
   d. Document any component-specific patterns or solutions
3. For complex or repeated patterns, use Tailwind's group syntax or consider component extraction.
4. For repeated utility combinations, use the `@apply` directive in component-specific CSS modules only when absolutely necessary.
5. Update any dynamic class generation logic to use Tailwind's conditional class utilities.
6. For responsive styles, use Tailwind's responsive prefixes (sm:, md:, lg:, etc.).
7. Testing approach: Compare each component visually before and after migration, and test across different viewport sizes to ensure responsive behavior is preserved.

subtasks.title: Remove Migrated Styles and Clean Up globals.css
subtasks.description: Incrementally remove unused or migrated styles from globals.css and verify that all styling is handled by Tailwind or component-scoped CSS.
subtasks.details:
1. Create a backup of the original globals.css file.
2. Based on the audit spreadsheet, mark each style as 'migrated' once its Tailwind equivalent has been applied to all affected components.
3. Group styles in globals.css by migration status (migrated vs. still needed).
4. Remove migrated styles in small batches, testing the application after each removal to ensure no visual regressions.
5. For any remaining necessary global styles that cannot be migrated to Tailwind (like third-party component styles or complex animations), consolidate them at the top of globals.css with clear comments.
6. Run the application in different browsers to verify cross-browser compatibility after style removal.
7. Use browser developer tools to confirm that removed styles are no longer being applied and that Tailwind classes are correctly rendering.
8. Testing approach: Create before/after screenshots of key pages and components to verify visual parity after style removal.

subtasks.title: Verify All Styling is Handled by Tailwind or Component-Scoped CSS
subtasks.description: Perform comprehensive testing to ensure all styling is properly handled by Tailwind or component-scoped CSS after globals.css cleanup.
subtasks.details:
1. Create a test plan covering all UI components and pages to verify styling integrity.
2. Systematically check each component to ensure all styles are properly applied through Tailwind classes or component-scoped CSS.
3. Test the application with globals.css completely disabled to identify any remaining dependencies.
4. For any styling issues discovered, determine whether they should be addressed with Tailwind utilities or component-scoped CSS.
5. Verify that all responsive behaviors are maintained across different viewport sizes.
6. Check all interactive states (hover, focus, active) to ensure they're correctly styled with Tailwind classes.
7. Test the application across different browsers to ensure cross-browser compatibility.
8. Create a final report documenting any remaining global CSS dependencies and why they couldn't be migrated.

tasks.title: Migrate PostList Component to Tailwind CSS
tasks.description: Refactor the PostList.tsx component to use Tailwind CSS utility classes instead of legacy or global CSS for all styling concerns including layout, spacing, and typography.
tasks.details:
This task involves migrating the existing PostList.tsx component located in src/components/ from its current CSS implementation to Tailwind CSS utility classes. The developer should:

1. Analyze the current component to identify all styling elements (margins, paddings, flexbox/grid layouts, colors, typography, etc.)
2. Replace all existing CSS class references with equivalent Tailwind utility classes
3. Remove any imports of CSS modules or stylesheets specific to this component
4. Ensure responsive behavior is maintained by using Tailwind's responsive prefixes (sm:, md:, lg:, etc.) where needed
5. Apply Tailwind's typography utilities for text styling (font sizes, weights, colors, line heights)
6. Use Tailwind's spacing utilities for margins and paddings
7. Implement Tailwind's flex or grid utilities for layout structures
8. Ensure hover states, transitions, and other interactive elements are preserved using Tailwind's state variants
9. Remove any inline styles and replace with Tailwind classes
10. Verify that no global CSS classes are being used in the component

The migration should be a direct styling conversion - functionality and component structure should remain unchanged.
tasks.testStrategy:
To verify the successful migration of the PostList component to Tailwind CSS:

1. Visual Inspection:
   - Compare screenshots of the component before and after migration to ensure visual parity
   - Verify the component looks correct at all responsive breakpoints (mobile, tablet, desktop)
   - Check that hover states and animations work as expected

2. Code Review:
   - Confirm all CSS class references have been replaced with Tailwind utilities
   - Verify no CSS imports remain in the component file
   - Ensure no inline styles are present
   - Check that no global CSS classes are being used

3. Functional Testing:
   - Verify the component renders correctly with different amounts of data
   - Test all interactive elements function as before
   - Ensure any conditional rendering still works properly

4. Browser Testing:
   - Test the component in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge to ensure cross-browser compatibility

5. Performance Check:
   - Compare bundle size before and after to ensure no significant increase
   - Verify render performance is maintained or improved

The task is complete when the component visually matches the original implementation, all tests pass, and no legacy CSS references remain in the code.
